ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a left-right symmetric geometric figure, with base AB being a horizontal line segment, A at the left end, B at the right end, and C above the perpendicular bisector of AB. Two large circular arcs from A and B respectively go upward and meet at C, forming an outer boundary similar to a curvilinear triangle. In the middle there is a relatively large inscribed circle, which is tangent to base AB near the midpoint, and is tangent to the two large circular arcs on the left and right respectively. Reasoning: According to the meaning of the problem, the center of arc AC is at B, so BA and BC are radii of the same circle, BA=BC. The center of arc BC is at A, so AB and AC are radii of the same circle, AB=AC. Therefore AB=AC=BC, and triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle with side length s. Arc BC has A as the center, and the corresponding central angle is ∠BAC=60°=π/3, so the arc length 12=s·π/3, obtaining s=36/π. Let A=(-s/2,0), B=(s/2,0). Since the figure is symmetric, the small inscribed circle is tangent to AB at the midpoint, and the center can be set as O=(0,r), where r is the radius of the small circle. The small circle is internally tangent to the large circular arc with A as the center and radius s, so AO=s-r. By the coordinate distance formula, AO^2=(s/2)^2+r^2. Thus (s/2)^2+r^2=(s-r)^2, simplifying gives s^2/4=s^2-2sr, so 2sr=3s^2/4, r=3s/8. The circumference of the required circle is 2πr=2π·3s/8=3πs/4. Substituting s=36/π, the circumference is 3π(36/π)/4=27.

First read the diagram as a symmetric curvilinear triangle with base AB horizontal, C above the midpoint, and the desired circle tangent to AB at the midpoint and tangent internally to the two large arcs. From the text, arc AC is centered at B and arc BC is centered at A, so AB=AC=BC=s and triangle ABC is equilateral. Therefore arc BC has central angle 60 degrees, so 12=s(pi/3), giving s=36/pi. Put A=(-s/2,0), B=(s/2,0), and let the small circle have center O=(0,r) because it is tangent to AB and symmetric. Since it is internally tangent to the circle centered at A of radius s, AO=s-r. 设 A=(-s/2,0)，B=(s/2,0)。由于图形对称，内切小圆与 AB 相切于中点，圆心可设为 O=(0,r)，其中 r 是小圆半径。小圆与以 A 为圆心、半径 s 的大圆弧内切，所以 AO=s-r。由坐标距离公式，AO^2=(s/2)^2+r^2。于是 (s/2)^2+r^2=(s-r)^2，化简得 s^2/4=s^2-2sr，所以 2sr=3s^2/4，r=3s/8。所求圆的周长为 2πr=2π·3s/8=3πs/4。代入 s=36/π，周长为 3π(36/π)/4=27。

method.method_draft: Use a geometric scale-ratio argument. From the image, note the figure is symmetric about the altitude through C and the midpoint M of AB, and the desired circle touches AB at M. From the text, because arc BC is centered at A and arc AC is centered at B, the endpoints satisfy AB=AC=BC=s, so ABC is equilateral and arc BC is one-sixth of its full generating circle. Thus the generating circle circumference is 6*12=72. Now determine the small-circle radius as a fraction of s without explicitly solving for s: let O be the small circle center and M the midpoint of AB. The tangency to AB gives OM=r; symmetry gives AM=s/2; internal tangency to the arc centered at A gives AO=s-r. In right triangle AMO, AM^2+OM^2=AO^2, so (s/2)^2+r^2=(s-r)^2 and r=3s/8. Therefore the small circle circumference is 3/8 of the generating circle circumference, namely (3/8)*72=27.

The center of arc BC is at A, so AB and AC are radii of the same circle, AB=AC. Therefore AB=AC=BC, and triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle with side length s. Arc BC has A as the center, and the corresponding central angle is ∠BAC=60°=π/3, so the arc length 12=s·π/3, obtaining s=36/π.

Let A=(-s/2,0), B=(s/2,0). Since the figure is symmetric, the small inscribed circle is tangent to AB at the midpoint, and the center can be set as O=(0,r), where r is the radius of the small circle. The small circle is internally tangent to the large circular arc with A as the center and radius s, so AO=s-r. By the coordinate distance formula, AO^2=(s/2)^2+r^2. Thus (s/2)^2+r^2=(s-r)^2, simplifying gives s^2/4=s^2-2sr, so 2sr=3s^2/4, r=3s/8. The circumference of the required circle is 2πr=2π·3s/8=3πs/4. Substituting s=36/π, the circumference is 3π(36/π)/4=27.
